text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Structured assessment: Y-BOCS symptom checklist and severity scale, PHQ-9, GAD-7, and AUDIT-C today; interview for tics, bipolar disorder, psychosis, hoarding, and body dysmorphic symptoms; thyroid, blood count, metabolic panel, albumin, and vitamin B12 for weight loss
  • Psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis, review comorbidity, and advise on sertraline dosing and the length of the trial
  • Exposure and response prevention with the clinic psychologist, weekly for 16 to 20 sessions, with a hierarchy he builds himself (touching door handles, shaking hands, eating without calculating, doing things in numbers other than three) and homework between sessions
  • Start sertraline 50 mg each morning; if the response is inadequate after four to six weeks, raise it in 50 mg steps every four to six weeks as tolerated, up to 200 mg, warning him about side effects and checking for them after each increase; judge the response only after eight to twelve weeks with at least four to six weeks at the top tolerated dose; continue for one to two years after a response
  • Collaborative safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people to contact, the clinic number, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; suicide-risk review at every visit
  • Nutrition: three fixed mealtimes, energy-dense foods he accepts, a session with the clinic dietitian, and weight at every visit; eating without calculating is an exposure target, not a rule imposed at the table
  • Hands: petrolatum after each wash and at night, cotton gloves overnight, nitrile gloves for laboratory solvents; cutting down washing is part of the exposure work
  • Sleep: a fixed six-to-seven-hour sleep window, no laboratory work after midnight, and a sleep diary
  • Respectful examination: explain each step and ask before touching; offer hand sanitizer, gloves, and paper covers before and after; let him wash if he wishes; no handshake expected; no unplanned exposures in clinic, which belong in therapy

resource.title: Nikola Tesla synthetic care plan
resource.description: Assess and treat severe obsessive-compulsive disorder in a 45-year-old electrical engineer, following the APA practice guideline (2007, with the 2013 guideline watch) and NICE CG31: a structured assessment with the Y-BOCS symptom checklist and severity scale, screening for depression, anxiety, tics, bipolar disorder, psychosis, and substance use, exposure and response prevention as first-line psychotherapy, sertraline raised in 50 mg steps to an effective dose, with the longer trial OCD needs, the effect of the rituals on his work, meals, sleep, and hands, an examination that respects his contamination fears without forcing exposures, and a structured suicide-risk assessment with a safety plan and the 988 Lifeline, while treating his historical rituals as his own accounts and not mocking or sensationalizing them.
